thread:
claire: RFC follow-up: how should the edge decide v3 vs v4 routing for tenants? Main options: explicit header, tenant flag, or runtime heuristics (probe + sticky). Need recommendation + rollout constraints.

jon: My vote is explicit header wins for correctness. Heuristic detection can be useful but should be opt-in via Console.

priya: Header-first is clean, but operationally many customers won't update quickly. Suggest: header > tenant-flag > probe. Probe should only run in shadow mode initially.

ben: Shadow-mode sounds right. Implementation caveat: if probe is allowed to flip routing automatically it must be reversible and rate-limited. Otherwise we risk flip-flopping under noise.

claire: Agreed. Propose sticky decisions with explicit TTL and change audit. Also want a canary path: route X% to v4 for N minutes and compare outputs.

jon: Canary idea: per-tenant canary with gradually increasing pct (1,5,25,100). Must capture "divergence score" metric. If divergence > threshold, abort canary.

priya: For probes we need deterministic small payloads to keep cost low. Recommend 3 probe inputs: system prompt (short), 1 context message, 1 embed request (small). Keep results for debugging only, scrub PII.

zhang: Telemetry: add metrics: routed_v4_pct, probe_pass_rate, probe_mismatch_rate, per_tenant_fallbacks. Export to Grafana and add alert when probe_mismatch_rate > 0.5% for 12h.

ben: Failure handling: if v4 returns 5xx or times out, immediately retry once to v3 then increment tenant cooldown counter. After M failures in T window, set tenant sticky->v3 and page.

claire: Nice. Also surface per-request header example: `X-Redwood-Infer-Compat: v3` (clients set to force old behavior). SDKs: ship middleware shim that can set header; default behavior should NOT set header until SDK major bump.

jon: SDK middleware will help adoption. For server-side SDKs we can provide a runtime flag that auto-injects header for legacy customers.

priya: Console UX: bulk-select tenants for opt-in/out, timeline of flips, text explaining risk, and an audit log showing who flipped what and why.

zhang: Data retention: probe payloads and diffs kept for 14 days, PII-scrubbed. Provide opt-out per-tenant (compliance). Store sampled payloads in secure bucket with KMS.

ben: Performance: tenant-config cache TTL = 3m by default. On miss, call tenant-config-service with 1ms p95 target. If service too slow, default route->v3 to avoid tail latency.

claire: Ops plan (rough weeks): Week A: enable shadow-mode + telemetry; Week B: SDK shim + header support; Week C: Console controls + batch API; Week D: gradual default for new tenants + canary automation; Week F: deprecation notices + final cutoff.

jon: I'll own canary automation and divergence scoring (ARC-3101).

priya: I'll own probe design and scrub pipeline (ARC-3102).

ben: I'll own routing edge changes and fallback logic (ARC-3103).

infra-bot: infra-bot: created ticket ARC-3101, ARC-3102, ARC-3103. Staging deploy scheduled for 2024-06-14T02:00:00Z.

claire: Final decision summary: priority order = 1) explicit header 2) tenant-config sticky decision (Console or batch API) 3) auto-detect probe only in shadow-first mode; safety = immediate fallback to v3 on v4 errors + cooldown; observability = divergence + mismatch metrics, sampled diffs, 14-day retention; SDK = middleware shim + docs. React with :+1: to accept or :eyes: to request changes.

jon: :+1:

priya: :+1:

ben: :+1:

zhang: :+1:
